title: Introduce adaptive causal sampling and SLO blame matrix
author: Priya Ramachandran
description:
Motivation: We see intermittent, low-volume SLO violations for token-latency on a small subset of tenants and model variants that do not show up in bulk rollups. Current full-trace capture is too expensive (both network and storage) to run continuously across all traffic. This PR introduces an adaptive causal sampling pipeline plus a lightweight SLO blame matrix to pinpoint likely causes (tenant, model variant, route, quantization profile, and KV-cache hit pattern) with low overhead.

What this PR does: Adds a streaming sampler that increases capture probability around candidate SLO breaches (latency & error-rate) while keeping baseline sampling low. Captures a compact causal fingerprint per sampled request (token-level latency distribution, model variant tag, tenant id hash, kv_cache_hit_ratio_binned, batch_size, dispatch_queue_depth). Adds an offline aggregator that computes a time-windowed SLO-blame matrix (rows: tenant cohort, cols: model variant/binary flags) with attribution scores and confidence intervals. Ships Grafana dashboard JSON and alert tuning recommendations to make on-call signals actionable.

Design notes: The sampler is policy-driven and executed in the edge-request-path instrumented code path with these constraints:
- baseline_sample_rate: 0.001 (0.1%)
- adaptive_boost_window_ms: 30000 (30s around detected candidate breach)
- max_boosted_rate_per_tenant: 0.05 (5%)
- cost_estimate: +2.4% ingest & +6% storage for traces in a medium-sized cluster (measured in dev cluster).

Sampling heuristics (implemented):
- Candidate breach if rolling_p99_latency(route, 1m) > route_slo_threshold * 0.9 OR request.error_count > 0.
- Boost a tenant-model pair for adaptive_boost_window_ms after a candidate breach with exponential backoff on repeated triggers.
- Reservoir-limited trace payloads: store only token-latency histogram (8 bins), first/last N tokens text (N=16), model variant, tenant hash, quantization_profile tag, kv_cache_hit_ratio_binned.

Aggregator & blame matrix: A lightweight reducer runs every 5m and computes:
- attribution_score = (breach_rate_cohort - baseline_breach_rate) * normalized_token_cost, aggregated with a Dirichlet-smoothed confidence interval.
- output: top-K tenant-model pairs with score, sample_count, estimated contribution percentage.
- persisted as time-series and as compact JSON blobs for dashboard join.

Dashboard & alerting: Adds a new Grafana dashboard (observability/slo-blame-matrix.json) with panels:
- SLO Blame matrix heatmap (PromQL-derived join of time-series + JSON blobs)
- Top-K causal traces table with contextual links to trace viewer
- Sampling rate heatmap and budget burn chart
Alert tuning guidance in docs: recommend replacing a single noisy route SLO alert with a composite that triggers only when attribution_confidence > 0.6 and sample_count > 20 to reduce pager noise.

Testing & validation:
- unit tests for sampler policy evaluation and reservoir limiter
- end-to-end test that injects synthetic breaches and validates that boosted sampling captures related traces with >90% recall in testbed
- load test (k8s cluster, 1m RPS synthetic) verifying <5% p99 latency regression on critical path and verifying estimated cost uplift.

Compatibility & rollout:
- Feature gate: observability.adaptive_causal_sampler (off by default)
- Gradual rollout plan: dev -> canary (2% users) -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with sampling budget telemetry monitored
- Backwards-compatible: aggregator tolerates missing enriched fields and falls back to cohort-level attribution when fine-grain data not available.

Related: Linked Linear work items ENG-4783, SRE-890; references: internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/slo-blame and grafana preview: https://grafana.internal/d/obs/slo-blame-matrix (preview).

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement sampler in edge path + reservoir limiter
- [x] Implement aggregator and attribution scoring
- [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON + screenshots
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs with rollout guidance

CI notes: Ran full unit/integration suite and microbenchmark harness; perf-noise within acceptable bounds (p99 +2.9% on sampler-enabled path in dev cluster, addressed by micro-optimization in commit 3).

Rollout/observability metrics to watch after merge: sampler.baseline_rate, sampler.boosted_rate, sampler.budget_burn, slo_blame.sample_count, slo_blame.attribution_score_leading_pairs.

Implementation caveats: The tenant identifier is stored as a 64-bit hash to avoid PII leakage. We intentionally do not persist raw prompt text past short snippet in the reservoir.

review_comments: Marco Li: Can we ensure the boosted window respects per-tenant budget caps? (resolved: added max_boosted_rate_per_tenant and budget_burn telemetry)
Anya Kostov: Aggregator Dirichlet smoothing looks good, but add note about small-sample bias. (author reply: added confidence interval and min_sample threshold of 5)
Benji Carter: Concern about extra CPU on aggregator, suggest offloading heavy math to batch job. (resolved: aggregator remains modest and uses compiled numpy; heavy joins deferred to async batch)
ci_checks: perf-regression: pass (p99 +2.9% in dev, within threshold)
release_notes: Adds an adaptive causal sampling pipeline and a SLO Blame Matrix dashboard that help correlate low-volume SLO breaches to tenant/model causes with low overhead. Feature gated and rolled out progressively. Includes docs and alert tuning guidance.
